title.en: US and Iran trade attacks as Khamenei is buried
title.zh: 美国和伊朗在哈梅内伊下葬期间互相攻击

summary.en: Centcom reported hitting 90 Iranian targets in the latest round of strikes, while the Iranian health ministry stated that 14 people had been killed since Tuesday.
summary.zh: 美国中央司令部报告称，在最新一轮袭击中，其打击了90个伊朗目标；伊朗卫生部表示，自周二以来已有14人死亡。

body.en:
The US and Iran again traded strikes in exchanges that continued into Thursday, as observers reported a "dramatic" drop in the number of ships travelling through the Strait of Hormuz.

The US says it hit 90 military targets, some near the Strait. Iran says 14 people have been killed in the past two days.

State media also reported that targets near the Bushehr nuclear power plant were hit, citing the deputy governor of the province. The US has not commented on the latest strikes.

Iran said it targeted US assets in Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar in response. Later on Thursday, Tehran launched more strikes on sites in Kuwait, Jordan and Iraq, state-linked media reported.

Separately, huge crowds gathered as Iran's late supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was buried after six days of funeral events.

Crowds massed on the streets of Mashhad in north-eastern Iran waving Iranian flags, while some were pictured holding signs carrying death threats directed at US President Donald Trump.

Khamenei was killed on 28 February during the first hours of US and Israeli strikes against Iran.

Bridges and a railway route connecting Tehran to the city of Mashhad, where the late supreme leader's funeral is being held, were also damaged, the foreign ministry said.

Iran's health ministry said 14 people had been killed and 78 people injured across five provinces.

Gulf nations reported Iranian attacks following the US strikes, with explosions in Bahrain's capital Manama, Kuwait intercepting missiles and drones, and Qatar issuing a security alert.

Later on Thursday, explosions were heard in Iran's southern port of Konarak, with a local official telling Iran's official news agency a navy site was attacked by an "enemy".

However a US defence official told the BBC it had not carried out any strikes in Iran in recent hours.

Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who is also the country's chief negotiator with the US, said on X that America "still hasn't learned that bullying and breaking promises are no longer cost-free".

"Let me put it plainly: if you strike, you'll get hit," he wrote, adding that the Strait of Hormuz will only open under Iranian arrangements - not "American threats".

US Central Command (Centcom) said the most recent round of strikes was carried out to "further degrade Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping and innocent civilian mariners" in the vital waterway.

In a statement, it said it had struck 90 Iranian military targets, which included air defense systems and military logistics infrastructure along Iran's coastline.

"The latest strikes follow successful execution of offensive strikes in Iran the night before," Centcom added.

title.en: Body of slain Iranian supreme leader arrives at Shi'ite shrine as crowds chant 'Kill Trump'

summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The funeral procession of Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has reached the country's holiest shrine for his burial as the crowd bore banners reading "We Will Kill Trump".

As a week of funeral events reached its culmination, Khamenei's son and successor Mojtaba Khamenei is still hidden from public view after being disfigured in the 28 Februarystrike that killed his father, a sign of the unease still gripping Iran.

Khamenei's body was carried by truck slowly through the crammed streets of Mashhad in northeastern Iran towards the gilt dome and minarets of the Shrine of Imam Reza, flanked by white-turbaned clerics. Black-clad mourners pressed in close behind, waving Iranian flags, photographs of the late Khamenei and red placards with revolutionary slogans.

A helicopter lifted his coffin the final short stretch with the truck unable to pass through the thick crowds. It then lay on a carpet as clerics stood praying behind.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Meanwhile hostilities with the United States have erupted again this week despite a truce, with Iran still controlling the vital Strait of Hormuz waterway and proclaiming its victory in having survived a months-long assault by its most powerful enemies, Israel and the US.

Iranian authorities are presenting Khamenei's burial and the huge crowds attending his funeral as evidence of the popularity of their theocratic state and its lasting ideological fire, nearly half a century after the 1979 Islamic revolution.

But beneath the surface, Iran faces huge internal challenges and the legacy of Khamenei's 37-year rule is bitterly disputed in a country where large numbers have repeatedly risen up to protest poverty and repression in recent years.

The whereabouts of Mojtaba Khamenei, proclaimed supreme leader by a clerical assembly in early March, a week after his father's death, has remained a mystery to Iranians.

He has not appeared in public since the war began with the strike that killed Ali Khamenei. While he has issued written statements, no image, video or voice recording of him has been issued.

He suffered debilitating injuries in that same strike, his face disfigured and limbs badly wounded.

Senior sources in Tehran have said he is recovering but that he has not yet been well enough to manage public appearances. State security services are also trying to limit his exposure in case of more attacks from the United States.

As crowds jostled in Mashhad awaiting Khamenei's funeral cortege, the crowd chanted slogans demanding revenge on US President Donald Trump for his killing.

title.en: Palestinians mourn Gaza World Cup screenings organiser killed in Israeli strike
title.zh: 巴勒斯坦人哀悼在以色列袭击中丧生的加沙世界杯放映组织者

summary.en: Aid worker Mohammed al-Wahidi had become a prominent humanitarian figure during the Israel-Hamas war.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The killing of Palestinian aid worker Mohammed al-Wahidi in an Israeli air strike in Gaza City on Tuesday has triggered an outpouring of grief across the Gaza Strip, where for many people he was one of the most recognisable humanitarian figures.

Within hours of his death, social media platforms were flooded with photographs and videos documenting his work, alongside hundreds of messages of condolence from people who said they had encountered him during aid distributions or while living in displacement camps.

An Israeli missile struck the taxi al-Wahidi was travelling in through the Sabra neighbourhood. He was killed along with three other people, including two brothers aged eight and 10 who were passing by and another man.

The Israeli military said it had struck a Hamas operative and was aware of claims that uninvolved individuals were killed in the strike.

Al-Wahidi, 65, was an English teacher before the war but became a senior official with the Egyptian Relief Committee in Gaza, an Egypt-backed organisation that has played a prominent role in humanitarian relief efforts in the Palestinian territory during the war between Israel and Hamas.

For more than two-and-a-half years he helped co-ordinate emergency food assistance, oversaw the establishment of camps for displaced families and worked to deliver aid to communities affected by repeated waves of displacement.

Many Gazans say he became a familiar face in shelters across the territory because he preferred to remain in the field rather than directing operations from an office.

Volunteers who worked alongside him describe a man who was regularly present at aid distribution points, speaking directly with displaced families and responding to their immediate needs.

In recent weeks, al-Wahidi became more widely known after helping organise public screenings of World Cup matches in Gaza City, Deir al-Balah and the al-Mawasi area in southern Gaza.

The initiative aimed to offer families, particularly children, a brief escape from the realities of war.

Egypt's matches attracted large crowds, reflecting the long-standing popularity of the team among many Palestinians in Gaza who have long shared cultural, emotional and political ties with their neighbours.

Videos of children and families gathering around giant screens among destroyed buildings spread widely online, offering rare scenes of celebration amid the conflict.

Al-Wahidi was killed only hours before one of those screenings, Egypt's last 16 match against Argentina, deepening the sense of loss among many Palestinians.

body.zh: 周二，巴勒斯坦援助人员穆罕默德·瓦希迪在以色列对加沙城的空袭中丧生，引发了整个加沙地带的悲痛，对许多人来说，他是最知名的人道主义人物之一。 在他去世后的几个小时内，社交媒体平台上充斥着记录他工作的照片和视频，还有数百条来自人们的哀悼信息，这些人说他们在分发援助物资或住在流离失所者营地时遇到了他。 一枚以色列导弹击中了瓦希迪在萨布拉街区行驶的出租车。他和另外三人一起被杀，其中包括路过的两名分别为八岁和十岁的兄弟和另一名男子。 以色列军方表示，它袭击了一名哈马斯特工，并了解有关无关人员在袭击中丧生的说法。 65 岁的瓦希迪在战前是一名英语教师，后来成为加沙埃及救援委员会的高级官员，该委员会是一个埃及支持的组织，在以色列和哈马斯之间的战争期间在巴勒斯坦领土的人道主义救援工作中发挥了重要作用。 在两年半多的时间里，他帮助协调紧急粮食援助，监督流离失所家庭营地的建立，并努力向受一波流离失所影响的社区提供援助。 许多加沙人表示，他成为该地区各地避难所的熟悉面孔，因为他更愿意留在现场，而不是在办公室指挥行动。 与他一起工作的志愿者描述了一名经常出现在援助分发点的男子，直接与流离失所的家庭交谈并满足他们的紧急需求。 最近几周，瓦希迪在帮助组织在加沙城、代尔巴拉赫和加沙南部的马瓦西地区公开放映世界杯比赛后变得更加出名。 该倡议旨在为家庭，特别是儿童，提供暂时逃离战争现实的机会。 埃及的比赛吸引了大批观众，这反映出该队长期以来在加沙地带的许多巴勒斯坦人中很受欢迎，他们长期以来与邻国有着文化、情感和政治联系。 儿童和家庭聚集在被摧毁的建筑物中的大屏幕周围的视频在网上广泛传播，提供了冲突中罕见的庆祝场景。 瓦希迪在其中一场放映前几个小时被杀，这场放映是埃及对阵阿根廷的最后 16 场比赛，加深了许多巴勒斯坦人的失落感。 “他不仅仅是人道主义委员会的一名援助工作者，”记录了瓦希迪工作的活动家穆罕默德·赫迈德写道。 “他是一扇希望之门，每天为流离失所者和失去亲人的人敞开......

title.en: Ukrainian agent accused of murdering Monaco bomb suspect changes story
title.zh: 被控谋杀摩纳哥炸弹嫌疑人的乌克兰特工改变了说法

summary.en: Two individuals with alleged ties to Ukraine's security services are accused of the murder of Anastasiia Berezovska, whose body was reportedly found in woods. One of the accused has reportedly altered his account of events.
summary.zh: 两名据称与乌克兰安全部门有关联的男子被指控谋杀阿纳斯塔西娅·别列佐夫斯卡娅，其尸体据报被发现于树林中。其中一名被告据报已改变了其对事件的陈述。

body.en:
A Ukrainian intelligence agent who confessed to killing the woman suspected of trying to assassinate a multimillionaire and his family in Monaco last week, has now claimed he did not pull the trigger.

In court in Kyiv for a custody hearing on Thursday, Vladyslav Reut – who a few days ago led investigators to Anastasiia Berezovska's grave in the woods – said that he "categorically denied" committing her murder and blamed his alleged accomplice instead.

This murky case is capturing attention because Reut is an active and decorated officer of Ukraine's military intelligence agency, GUR, and his co-defendant Vitalii Zhykovych worked for the SBU security service until recently.

On Thursday evening President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would have "additional relevant reports" to share in the coming days.

But the motive for the Monaco blast that targeted Vadym Yermolayev remains unclear.

​The businessman, who made his money in cognac and real estate, had renounced his Ukrainian citizenship some years ago. He has since been sanctioned by Kyiv for continuing to do business in Crimea after it was taken by Russia.

The two suspects were brought into court for separate hearings with their hands cuffed, surrounded by heavily armed security officers in balaclavas.

Both kept their hoods up throughout proceedings and their faces covered by masks so large only their eyes were still visible. They sat hunched inside the glass courtroom cage for most of the hearings, backs to the line of TV cameras.

In court, the prosecutor clarified that Anastasiia Berezovska had arrived in Ukraine two days after the blast in Monaco, and before she had been identified as the prime suspect in the case.

Once alerted to the allegations against her, investigators seem to have honed in quickly on Zhykovych, 50, and Reut, 34, using Berezovska's phone records.

They then identified cash and cryptocurrency transfers that the two had made to her accounts.

He then took investigators to the spot where he had buried her body in the woods west of Kyiv, in a grave covered with branches.

But in court just days later, the GUR agent announced that he wanted to "tell the truth". He then shifted the blame squarely onto Zhykovych.

"I fought enemy combatants while defending my country," he stressed. "I would never intentionally murder an innocent civilian woman."

In his revised version, he claimed that the two men had driven in his BMW to pick up Berezovska on the highway to Kyiv because she "needed to be hidden" in connection with "a criminal matter".

On the way, Reut says Zhykovych produced a modified Makarov pistol from his rucksack and loaded it. When he protested, he says Zhykovych claimed it was just a precaution "in case she panics".

title.en: What's next for Iran after the funeral of their late supreme leader?
title.zh: 伊朗已故最高领袖葬礼后，该国将走向何方？

summary.en: Following the funeral of their late supreme leader, Iran's new leadership is now tasked with addressing various national issues. The BBC's chief international correspondent is examining how these new leaders will navigate the country's future challenges.
summary.zh: 在已故最高领袖的葬礼之后，伊朗新领导层面临着处理影响该国的各种问题。英国广播公司首席国际记者正在审视这些新领导人将如何应对国家未来的挑战。

body.en:
After a week of mass funeral processions, rallies and mourning ceremonies in Iran, the assassinated former supreme leader has been buried .

Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the US-Israeli war, but his funeral was delayed because of the ongoing conflict that saw senior iranian figured targeted and killed.

He was succeeded as supreme leader by his son Mojtaba, who has not been seen in public since he was reportedly wounded in the same attack.

The BBC's chief international correspondent, Lyse Doucet, looks at how Iran's new leadership will respond to several issues affecting the country.
body.zh: 经过一周的大规模葬礼游行、集会和哀悼仪式，伊朗被暗杀的前最高领袖被埋葬。 阿亚图拉阿里·哈梅内伊在美以战争开始时被杀，但由于冲突持续不断，伊朗高级人物成为攻击目标并被杀害，他的葬礼被推迟。 他的最高领导人职位由他的儿子莫吉塔巴接替，自从据报道他在同一次袭击中受伤以来，莫吉塔巴就没有在公开场合露面。 BBC 首席国际记者 Lyse Doucet 探讨伊朗新领导层将如何应对影响该国的几个问题。

reflection.en: As Iran's new leadership steps into its role, the weight of national issues demands profound wisdom in decision-making. In times of transition and uncertainty, leaders and citizens alike can seek Yahweh for the discernment needed to navigate complex challenges.
reflection.zh: 随着伊朗新领导层就职，国家面临的诸多问题要求他们在决策上展现出深刻的智慧。在过渡和不确定的时期，领导者和公民都可以向雅伟寻求洞察力，以应对复杂的挑战。

verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: South Africa: Driven home by anti-migrant protests
title.zh: 南非：因反移民抗议活动被迫返乡

summary.en: Two women shared their experiences of being forced to leave South Africa and return to Zambia due to anti-migrant protests, having to restart their lives from nothing.
summary.zh: 两名妇女讲述了她们因南非的反移民抗议活动而被迫离开南非返回赞比亚，不得不从头开始重建生活的故事。

body.en:
Two women tell DW how anti-migrant protests upended their lives in South Africa, forcing them to return to Zambia and rebuild from scratch.

With her baby strapped to her back and carrying little more than the clothes she was wearing, Glenda Banda crossed back into Zambia amid growing anti-migrant sentiment in South Africa .

South Africa has been her home for a decade. It was where she found work, raised her family and hoped to build a better future. She told DW that within days, everything she had worked for was gone.

"I came with only the clothes on my body. I had no clothes to change into," Banda said, adding that the local mayor had sent young men to her home to ask the landlord to evict her and her family.

"The landlord was forced to put all our belongings outside and lock the house," Banda told DW. "We had to flee and leave everything behind."

Banda is among more than 100 Zambians who returned to their homeland after anti-migrant protests — some of which turned violent — called for migrants  to be sent back.

Bernadette Mwelwa tells a similar story. After living in South Africa for more than 20 years, she returned to Zambia having lost not only her livelihood but also the life she had built there.

"Even if you were a refugee or an asylum seeker , as long as you were a foreigner they didn't want us there," she said.

"I can't go back to South Africa because I lost a lot of things. The mayor took the keys to my salon," Mwelwa told DW. "I left my husband, who is Congolese, to look after our supermarket, but it was looted and everything is gone."

Nigeria, Mozambique and Ghana have all raised concerns about attacks on their citizens living in South Africa.

Nigeria  on Sunday denounced the deaths of two of its citizens in South Africa , warning that foreign nationals are being "unduly targeted" amid the anti-migrant protests. South Africa's main police watchdog said it had opened an investigation, Reuters reported.

Mozambique's government said five of its citizens were killed "as a direct consequence of the xenophobic attacks" that flared after a march against undocumented migrants in the South African town of Mossel Bay at the end of May. 

South African police ​said only two Mozambicans died after being assaulted following the march, and would not say if there was a link with anti-migrant sentiment, according to the news agency Associated Press. 

Ghana said last week one of its citizens was fatally wounded in a shooting during the anti-migrant demonstrations. South Africa said his killing was not related to the protests ​and accused Ghana of spreading misinformation .

body.zh: 两名妇女告诉德国之声，反移民抗议活动如何颠覆了她们在南非的生活，迫使她们返回赞比亚并从头开始重建。 格伦达·班达（Glenda Banda）背着孩子，除了身上穿的衣服外，几乎没有带任何东西，在南非反移民情绪日益高涨的情况下，她穿越回赞比亚。 十年来，南非一直是她的家。她在那里找到了工作，养育了家庭，并希望建立更美好的未来。她告诉德国之声，几天之内，她为之努力的一切都消失了。 班达说：“我只带着身上的衣服。我没有衣服可换。”她补充说，当地市长派了年轻人到她家，要求房东驱逐她和她的家人。 班达告诉德国之声：“房东被迫把我们所有的物品都放在外面，并锁上房子。” “我们不得不逃离并抛下一切。” 班达是在反移民抗议活动（其中一些抗议活动演变成暴力活动）要求遣返移民后返回祖国的 100 多名赞比亚人之一。 伯纳黛特·姆韦尔瓦 (Bernadette Mwelwa) 也讲述了类似的故事。在南非生活了20多年后，她回到赞比亚，不仅失去了生计，也失去了在那里建立的生活。 “即使你是难民或寻求庇护者，只要你是外国人，他们就不希望我们在那里，”她说。 姆韦尔瓦告诉德国之声：“我无法回到南非，因为我失去了很多东西。市长拿走了我沙龙的钥匙。” “我留下我的刚果人丈夫来照看我们的超市，但超市被洗劫一空，所有东西都消失了。” 尼日利亚、莫桑比克和加纳都对居住在南非的本国公民遭受袭击表示担忧。 尼日利亚周日谴责了两名尼日利亚公民在南非的死亡事件，并警告称，外国人在反移民抗议活动中成为“不当目标”。据路透社报道，南非主要警察监管机构表示已展开调查。 莫桑比克政府表示，五月底南非莫塞尔湾镇针对无证移民的游行后爆发的“仇外袭击直接导致”五名莫桑比克公民被杀。 据美联社报道，南非警方表示，只有两名莫桑比克人在游行后遭到袭击而死亡，并且不愿透露是否与反移民情绪有关。 加纳上周表示，一名公民在反移民示威期间的枪击事件中身亡。南非表示他的被杀与抗议活动无关​并指责加纳散布错误信息。 尽管许多移民仍留在南非，但在经历了数周的反移民情绪、威胁以及在一些地区……之后，数千人离开了南非。

reflection.en: The displacement of these women highlights the pain caused when communities reject those seeking a new home. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to treat foreigners as native-born, loving them as ourselves, remembering our shared human vulnerability. This principle calls us to extend compassion and justice to all, regardless of their origin.
reflection.zh: 这些妇女的流离失所凸显了当社区排斥寻求新家园的人时所造成的痛苦。雅伟古老的诫命提醒我们，要善待寄居者如同本地人，爱他们如同爱自己，并记住我们共同的人性脆弱。这一原则呼吁我们对所有人，无论其出身如何，都施以怜悯和公义。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Congo: UN laments uptick in fighting in South Kivu
title.zh: 刚果：联合国哀叹南基伍省战事升级

summary.en: The UN human rights chief has urged an immediate end to intensified clashes between the army and the Rwanda-backed M23 militia in South Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
summary.zh: 联合国人权事务高级专员呼吁刚果民主共和国东部南基伍省的军队与卢旺达支持的M23民兵组织之间日益激烈的冲突立即停止。

body.zh: 联合国人权事务高级专员呼吁立即停止刚果民主共和国东部的战斗。此前，军队与卢旺达支持的“M23”民兵在南基伍省发生了激烈冲突。 联合国人权事务高级专员沃尔克·蒂尔克周四呼吁各方停止在刚果民主共和国东部的敌对行动。 过去两周，刚果民主共和国武装部队与卢旺达军队支持的“M23”武装团体在南基伍边境地区的战斗愈演愈烈。 至少自 2021 年“M23”运动重新出现并在数十年来饱受冲突困扰的边境地区夺取大片领土以来，这场斗争一直在消退。 蒂尔克对最近南基伍省冲突对平民造成的影响表示遗憾，呼吁国家和国际社会共同努力缓和紧张局势。 图尔克说：“令人深感不安的是，尽管作为正在进行的和平进程的一部分达成了协议，但刚果民主共和国东部的战斗仍然有增无减——造成平民伤亡、流离失所，生计遭到破坏。” 尽管去年底在多哈达成了和平框架协议并受到美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的赞扬，但 7 月 4 日至 5 日，菲齐的穆利马村周围仍发生了激烈的冲突，但该协议在制止战斗方面的行动相对较少。 图尔克表示：“我敦促刚果武装部队和‘3·23’运动立即停止进一步的暴力活动，并采取紧急行动缓和紧张局势。” “我还呼吁双方采取有意义的措施，保护穆利马以及更广泛的菲齐和姆文加高原地区的平民。在人口稠密地区使用具有大范围杀伤力的爆炸性武器会造成毁灭性后果，必须停止。” 图尔克办公室还在声明中表示，他“敦促卢旺达停止对“3·23”运动的支持，并从刚果民主共和国撤军”，同时敦促刚果民主共和国“加大”努力，“复员、解除武装和遣返卢旺达民主力量（FDLR）成员”，尽管没有直接引用奥地利官员的话。 联合国怀疑双方在最近南基伍省的战斗中都犯有战争罪。 南基伍省是刚果民主共和国的一个边境地区，与卢旺达接壤，富含黄金、锡矿石和钶钽矿储量，两国最近的共同历史极为紧张。 卢旺达内战，特别是 20 世纪 90 年代初的种族灭绝之后，数百万胡图族人——包括一些参与大规模屠杀图西族的人——逃到了当时被称为扎伊尔的地方。卢旺达及其盟国因此在1996年发起进攻，基加利也深度参与了第一次和第二次刚果战争……

reflection.en: The ongoing conflict in eastern Congo reminds us of the deep human longing for an end to violence. In times when peace seems elusive, we hold onto the hope that Yahweh is ultimately the one who can make wars cease. May this hope inspire continued efforts for reconciliation and stability in the region.
reflection.zh: 刚果东部持续的冲突提醒我们人类对暴力止息的深切渴望。在和平看似遥不可及的时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟最终能使战争止息的盼望。愿这盼望激励该地区持续的和解与稳定努力。

title.en: Iran after Khamenei: A new order takes shape
title.zh: 哈梅内伊之后的伊朗：新秩序正在形成

summary.en: Mojtaba Khamenei has become Iran's new supreme leader, inheriting a political system that his father spent decades developing and molding to his own vision.
summary.zh: 莫吉塔巴·哈梅内伊已成为伊朗新任最高领袖，他继承了其父数十年来建立并塑造成自己形象的政治体系。

body.en:
Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's new supreme leader, has inherited a political system that his father spent decades building and shaping in his own image.

The Islamic Republic of Iran is entering a new political era as Iranians on Thursday prepared to bury their slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in his hometown of Mashhad in northeastern Iran.  

His son and successor Mojtaba Khamenei still remains hidden from public view after being disfigured in the US air strike that killed his father when the Iran war began on February 28.

The younger Khamenei — the Islamic Republic's third supreme leader since the 1979 Revolution — was conspicuously absent from even the official mourning ceremonies for his father.

This leadership transition in Iran represents far more than a simple change at the top of the state.

It is the culmination of a profound institutional transformation that unfolded during Ali Khamenei's nearly four decades in power.

Reza Talebi, a political analyst, said Khamenei gradually reshaped the power structures of the Islamic Republic.

"Unlike Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, who established a system after the revolution that rested on revolutionary legitimacy and his personal authority, Ali Khamenei began systematically restructuring that system,” Talebi told DW.

Over the past 37 years, the influence of senior clerics and Shiite semnaries over key political decisions has steadily diminished , he pointed out. In their place, security institutions, the Office of the Supreme Leader, and the political and military networks associated with it have become increasingly dominant, the expert added.

This transformation has also altered the role of Iran's elected institutions. In Talebi's view, presidential elections have increasingly evolved into contests conducted within a pre-defined political framework.

Although presidents from different political factions were able to pursue their own domestic priorities, they had limited room for maneuver in strategic areas such as foreign policy, the nuclear program, and regional affairs, Talebi said.

Notably, during the six-day state mourning ceremonies for Ali Khamenei, none of the Islamic Republic's three former living presidents — Hassan Rouhani, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad , and Mohammad Khatami —appeared alongside other leading figures of the political establishment.

Instead, official images focused on representatives of the security apparatus, particularly commanders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), as well as incumbent President Masoud Pezeshkian.

Pezeshkian is widely believed to have maintained a close working relationship with Mojtaba Khamenei. He played a central role in negotiations aimed at ending the Iran war.

body.zh: 伊朗新任最高领袖莫吉塔巴·哈梅内伊继承了其父亲花费数十年时间按照自己的形象建立和塑造的政治制度。 伊朗伊斯兰共和国正在进入一个新的政治时代，伊朗人周四准备在伊朗东北部的家乡马什哈德埋葬被杀的最高领袖阿亚图拉·阿里·哈梅内伊。 2 月 28 日伊朗战争爆发时，他的儿子兼继任者莫吉塔巴·哈梅内伊 (Mojtaba Khamenei) 在美国空袭中被毁容，导致其父亲身亡，至今仍隐藏在公众视线之外。 年轻的哈梅内伊——自 1979 年革命以来伊斯兰共和国的第三位最高领导人——甚至明显缺席了其父亲的官方哀悼仪式。 伊朗的领导层换届不仅仅意味着国家高层的简单变动。 这是阿里·哈梅内伊执政近四十年期间展开的深刻制度变革的顶峰。 政治分析家礼萨·塔莱比表示，哈梅内伊逐渐重塑了伊斯兰共和国的权力结构。 塔莱比告诉德国之声：“阿亚图拉鲁霍拉·霍梅尼在革命后建立了一个基于革命合法性和个人权威的体系，而阿里·哈梅内伊则开始系统性地重组该体系。” 他指出，过去37年里，高级神职人员和什叶派神学院对关键政治决策的影响力不断减弱。专家补充说，取而代之的是安全机构、最高领袖办公室以及与之相关的政治和军事网络，它们已变得越来越占主导地位。 这一转变也改变了伊朗民选机构的作用。在塔勒比看来，总统选举越来越演变成在预先确定的政治框架内进行的竞争。 塔莱比表示，尽管来自不同政治派别的总统能够追求自己的国内优先事项，但他们在外交政策、核计划和地区事务等战略领域的回旋余地有限。 值得注意的是，在阿里·哈梅内伊为期六天的国家哀悼仪式上，伊斯兰共和国三位在世前总统——哈桑·鲁哈尼、马哈茂德·艾哈迈迪内贾德和穆罕默德·哈塔米——都没有与政治机构的其他领导人一起出现。 相反，官方形象集中在安全机构的代表上，特别是伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）的指挥官，以及现任总统马苏德·佩泽什基安。 人们普遍认为佩泽什基安与莫杰塔巴·哈梅内伊保持着密切的工作关系。他在旨在结束伊朗战争的谈判中发挥了核心作用。 这场冲突于 2 月 28 日开始，与美国和...

reflection.en: As a new leader steps into power, the character of governance profoundly shapes the lives of a nation's people. Yahweh's word reminds us that the well-being of a society is deeply connected to the integrity and nature of its leadership.
reflection.zh: 当一位新领袖掌权时，治理的品格深刻地影响着一个民族的生活。雅伟的话语提醒我们，一个社会的福祉与领导层的正直和本质息息相关。

title.en: Iran strikes military sites in Gulf states after top negotiator's warning against US 'bullying'

summary.en: The attacks on Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain followed recent US strikes on Iran's southern coastal and eastern provinces.

body.en:
Iranian armed forces targeted United States military infrastructure in neighbouring Gulf states on Thursday following US strikes on Iran's southern coastal and eastern provinces, putting further strain on a three-week-old ceasefire agreement.

Iran was also preparing on Thursday to bury its slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the country's holiest shrine in Mashhad, in the northeast, the culmination of a week of mass funeral processions and rallies. Khamenei was killed in a US airstrike on the first day of the war on 28 February.

The US military said on Wednesday its latest strikes on Iran were aimed at keeping the Strait of Hormuz open after Iran targeted three tankers in the area.

The assault came hours after US President Donald Trump said he believed the interim ceasefire with Iran to be "over".

Iranian officials said the US attacks had killed 14 people and injured 78 across five provinces on 8 and 9 July, state media reported. The Fars news agency said one US strike had hit a rail bridge used for trade with Russia and China.

Several explosions were heard on Thursday morning in Iran's Bushehr province, the semi-official Mehr news agency reported. Bushehr is home to a Russian-built nuclear power plant.

Iran's army said in a statement released by state media that it had targeted US Patriot systems with drones in Kuwait, an early warning site in Qatar (satellite antenna) and a fuel storage facility of the US army in Bahrain.

Kuwait said its armed forces had engaged with a cruise missile, three ballistic missiles and 10 drones in its airspace, and that one person had been injured from falling shrapnel.

Qatar, which hosts the largest US military base in the region and has often mediated between Washington and its adversaries, including Tehran, called for a return to diplomacy.

In a phone call with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi, Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani also condemned attacks targeting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

While Iran has not claimed responsibility for the ship attacks, analysts say Tehran uses such actions to gain leverage in negotiations.

The Strait of Hormuz handled about a fifth of global oil supplies before the war erupted on 28 February with US and Israeli strikes against Iran.

Tehran has since taken effective control of the strait, allowing it to force a stalemate in its confrontation with the world's most powerful military.

title.en: Uranium, universities, and 'top-tier' security: Inside the new Albanese-Modi agreements
title.zh: 铀、大学和“顶级”安全：阿尔巴尼亚-莫迪新协议的内幕

summary.en: Rivals in cricket, but allies in defence. Here's what the two nations have committed to.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及合一、和好与弥合分歧。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A handshake and a smile sealed the deal between Australia and its "top-tier" security partner, as Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, pledged to strengthen ties across trade, education, defence, science and technology.

" While we are separated by an ocean, we are indeed the closest of friends," Albanese told reporters in Canberra during a joint press statement.

"Australia values India as a top-tier security partner, and the Declaration reflects our shared commitment to a peaceful, stable and prosperous Indo-Pacific region."

References to cricket embraced the common ground between the two nations, with Modi likening their partnership to a "long and intense test match".

However, underneath the sports metaphors was an undercurrent of concern around the Indo-Pacific's defence challenges, with one eye on the fallout of war in Iran and economic disruptions, and the other on China, just days after it conducted a missile test in the Pacific .

title.en: Is the Strait of Hormuz still Iran's trump card?
title.zh: 霍尔木兹海峡仍是伊朗的王牌吗？

summary.en: Iran's recent actions demonstrate its capacity to disrupt global shipping and energy markets, potentially drawing in neighboring Gulf states. The article examines Iran's actual leverage over Washington and the possible repercussions of its high-risk approach.

body.en:
Iran's latest attacks show it can easily disrupt shipping, energy markets and draw in Gulf neighbors. DW asks how much leverage Tehran really has over Washington and if its high-risk strategy could backfire.

The Iran war has reignited after Tehran struck at least three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to US and maritime officials.

The attacks, which targeted a Saudi oil tanker and a Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier, prompted the United States  to revoke the temporary sanctions waiver on Iranian oil exports.

This major concession in the memorandum of understanding (MOU) agreed by the US and Iran last month allowed Tehran to restart oil exports after its tankers were halted by a US Navy blockade.

In further retaliation, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said Wednesday it had struck more than 80 targets in Iran, including air defense systems, radars and over 60 small boats used by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to harass shipping .

The US military said it followed up Thursday with a fresh round of strikes on around 90 targets.

CENTCOM said it wanted to "impose heavy costs for targeting and attacking commercial shipping crewed by innocent civilians in an international waterway."

Iran then hit back by launching fresh missile strikes on Gulf nations on Wednesday, with air raid sirens and explosions reported in Bahrain and Kuwait . Further strikes were reported Thursday.

Traffic through the strait, which had restarted after the ceasefire deal, had again grinded to a halt, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing shipping tracking data.

Reacting to the escalation, maritime security firm MARISKS warned Wednesday that the tit-for-tat action "marks a return to direct military confrontation."

Speaking ahead of a NATO summit in Turkey, US President Donald Trump said the MOU with Iran was now "over," adding that "It’s just a waste of time dealing with them [Tehran]."

China and Qatar, meanwhile, called for an immediate de-escalation, while German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius called on Tehran to stop provoking Washington and cease attacks on vessels.

Iran is trying to maintain its control over Hormuz, the narrow waterway that before the war carried a fifth of the world's oil and gas exports from the Gulf to the rest of the world.

Iran effectively closed the strait after US-Israeli airstrikes killed several Iranian officials, including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei , on February 28. Later, Iran struck around a dozen ships caught in the strait, before a fragile ceasefire deal was reached last month.

body.en:
One of the "world's best missiles" could be manufactured in Ukraine as part of its defence against Russia, but experts say it's only good news "down the road" for the war-torn nation.

Speaking at a NATO summit overnight, United States President Donald Trump offered to give Ukraine a licence to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

The missiles are one of the only weapons capable of countering Russia's most brutal attacks, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has been asking for them for years and more recently for a licence to manufacture them.

Russian ballistic missile strikes have killed dozens of Ukrainians in the past week and caused significant damage to infrastructure.

While Trump's offer could be a lifeline to Ukraine, it could be too little and too late in its war with Russia, as the president also considers his relationship with other world leaders.

Patriot missiles are a little over 5m in length, 40cm in diameter, and have a range of 70km, the Associated Press reports.

The missiles are fired from a battery that costs approximately $US10 million ($14.4 million) to manufacture and can require as many as 90 troops to operate and maintain it.

Oleksandra Molloy, a senior lecturer in aviation safety at the University of New South Wales, told SBS News that the Patriots are widely regarded as among the world's most capable air defence missiles.

"They are very effective at downing incoming ballistic missiles, which fly at much higher altitudes and are much faster than other types of missiles or drones," she said.

The US has previously provided these missiles to Ukraine for its defence, but intelligence suggests the country now has limited means to defend against Russian strikes.

Douglas Lute, a former US ambassador to NATO, said it's likely Ukraine has run out of defensive missiles, leaving it vulnerable.

"Recently, none of the incoming Russian ballistic missiles has been downed. That suggests that Ukraine is essentially out of its Patriot air defence system," he told ABC Radio National on Thursday morning.

When asked if the United States would send additional Patriot interceptors immediately, Trump said "some" could be sent immediately and that he thought Ukraine could begin to produce its own quickly.

"We have Patriots, but we don't have that many. We need them for ourselves too," he said.

Lute estimated that it takes the US around two years to produce the defensive missiles, saying that while Ukraine has a strong defence industry, manufacturing Patriots could be a challenge.

title.en: Factory fire kills at least 28 in China's 'shoe capital'
title.zh: 中国“鞋都”工厂火灾造成至少28人死亡

summary.en: Footage shows huge flames rising from a building and thick, black smoke rising into the sky.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A fire at a shoe factory in the south-eastern Chinese city of Jinjiang has killed at least 28 people, according to the state news agency.

Dramatic footage posted by Xinhua showed huge plumes of black smoke rising from a building as well as people who appeared to be trapped on the roof.

President Xi Jinping said the blaze had caused "major casualties", adding those responsible must be held "strictly accountable".

Jinjiang, in the province of Fujian, is often referred to as China's "shoe capital" as it reportedly manufactures 20% of the world's sports shoes.

The blaze erupted at the Huiteng Footwear factory at around noon local time (05:00 BST) on Thursday.

Hundreds of rescue workers were rushed to the scene, state broadcaster CCTV reports, and more than 200 people were evacuated.

Initial reports suggest the fire may have started on the factory's ground floor where flammable materials were stored.

Authorities have detained a number of people who work for the factory's owners, and the firm's bank account was frozen, according to Xinhua.

China started a campaign to prevent fires in high-rise buildings after a blaze ripped through several Hong Kong apartment buildings in November , killing 168 people.

summary.en: Hundreds of rescue workers were dispatched to the site in Jinjiang, China, where many had become trapped in a burning factory. President Xi Jinping said "heavy human losses" were expected.

body.en:
Hundreds of rescue workers were dispatched to the site in Jinjiang, China, where many had become trapped in a burning factory. President Xi Jinping said "heavy human losses" were expected.

At least 28 people were killed in a fire at a shoe factory in eastern China on Thursday.

China's Ministry of Emergency Management announced that some 200 fire and rescue workers had been dispatched to a shoe factory in Fujian province on Thursday.

President Xi Jinping has called for "an all-out search and rescue effort" and a swift investigation in order to "strictly hold those responsible accountable."

Dozens of fire trucks were seen dumping water on the burnt multi-story factory as smoke continued to billow from the site.

"Simultaneously, the cause of the fire must be investigated, lessons learned, and effective measures taken to prevent similar accidents from recurring," the ministry said in a statement.

Beijing launched a renewed campaign to bring high-rise buildings and factories in line with fire codes in November after 168 people were killed in Hong Kong where several tower blocks went up in flames.
body.zh: 数百名救援人员被派往中国晋江的现场，许多人被困在一座着火的工厂里。习近平主席表示，预计将造成“严重人员伤亡”。 周四，中国东部一家鞋厂发生火灾，造成至少 28 人死亡。 中国应急管理部周四宣布，已派出约200名消防救援人员前往福建省一家鞋厂。 习近平主席呼吁“全力搜救”，迅速展开调查，“严肃追究责任人的责任”。 人们看到数十辆消防车向被烧毁的多层工厂倾倒水，现场浓烟继续滚滚。 公安部在一份声明中表示：“同时，必须调查起火原因，吸取教训，并采取有效措施，防止类似事故再次发生。” 11 月，香港多座高楼起火，导致 168 人死亡，北京方面重新启动了一项行动，要求高层建筑和工厂遵守消防规范。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到领导、智慧与公共责任。Proverbs 11:14提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以智慧、正直与服事来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Venomous snakes escape breeding farms in southern China during flooding
title.zh: 中国南方洪灾中，毒蛇从养殖场逃逸

summary.en: Hundreds of snakes, including king ratsnakes and cobras, have escaped from flooded breeding farms in southern China. This incident occurred as severe storms, including typhoon Maysak, caused widespread flooding in the region.
summary.zh: 中国南方多地遭受严重风暴袭击，台风“美莎克”引发洪水，导致数百条蛇，包括王锦蛇和眼镜蛇，从被淹的养殖场逃逸。

body.en: Local media in Hengzhou report king ratsnakes and cobras among hundreds in flood waters caused by typhoon Maysak Hundreds of snakes, including cobras, have escaped from flooded breeding farms in southern China as severe storms continue to batter parts of the country. State media reported that a snake farm in Hengzhou, in Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region, was hit by flood waters after days of heavy rainfall caused by typhoon Maysak , prompting warnings for nearby residents. Continue reading...
body.zh: 衡州当地媒体报道称，台风“美莎克”引发的洪水中，有数百条蛇王和眼镜蛇。随着严重风暴继续袭击中国部分地区，包括眼镜蛇在内的数百条蛇从中国南部被洪水淹没的养殖场中逃出。官方媒体报道称，台风“美莎”连日来带来强降雨，广西壮族自治区横州的一个养蛇场遭到洪水袭击，附近居民收到警告。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The escape of venomous snakes during severe flooding reminds us of creation's vulnerability when faced with powerful natural forces. Romans 8:22 speaks to how the whole creation groans under the weight of disruption, a reality keenly felt when disasters lead to unexpected dangers. In such times, we are called to care for both human safety and the wider...
reflection.zh: 毒蛇在严重洪水中逃逸，提醒我们面对强大自然力量时，受造界的脆弱性。罗马书8:22提到整个受造界都在劳苦叹息，当灾难带来意想不到的危险时，这种感受尤为强烈。在这样的时刻，我们蒙召要关顾人类安全和更广阔的自然界，信靠雅伟最终的掌权。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Typhoon, tornadoes, landslides: deadly weather ravages China – in pictures
title.zh: 台风、龙卷风、山体滑坡：致命天气肆虐中国（图）

summary.en: Typhoon Maysak and severe storms, including tornadoes and landslides, have caused widespread devastation across China, resulting in at least 15 fatalities in Guangxi and Hubei provinces.
summary.zh: 台风“美莎克”和包括龙卷风、山体滑坡在内的严重风暴在中国各地造成了广泛破坏，导致广西和湖北省至少15人死亡。

reflection.en: In the face of devastating natural disasters like typhoons and tornadoes, human vulnerability is starkly revealed. Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Even amidst the chaos and loss, we can find solace in the enduring presence of the Divine.
reflection.zh: 面对台风和龙卷风等毁灭性的自然灾害，人类的脆弱性显露无遗。诗篇46:1提醒我们，雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。即使在混乱和损失之中，我们也能在神永恒的同在中找到慰藉。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: German car industry warns of job collapse unless ‘bold decisions’ made to address Chinese threat
title.zh: 德国汽车工业警告称，除非做出“大胆决定”应对中国威胁，否则将面临就业岗位崩溃

summary.en: The German car industry has issued a stark warning about a potential collapse of employment in the sector across Europe, proposing up to 100,000 job losses at Volkswagen and suggesting that car plants might need to be placed under foreign ownership to safeguard remaining jobs amidst growing competition from China.
summary.zh: 德国汽车工业发出严峻警告，称除非做出“大胆决定”以应对来自中国的威胁，否则欧洲汽车行业的就业岗位可能面临崩溃。大众汽车公司提议裁员多达10万人，并表示为保住剩余工作岗位，汽车工厂可能需要由外国公司持有。

body.en: VW to propose 100,000 job losses to board and says car plants could be put under foreign ownership to save jobs Europe live – latest updates The German car industry has warned of a potential collapse of employment in the sector in Europe unless society and workers accept that “bold decisions” are needed to address competition from the Chinese and other rivals. Volkswagen is preparing to formally propose up to 100,000 job losses , a move that has triggered a wave of protests. Continue reading...
body.zh: 大众汽车提议裁员10万人，并表示汽车工厂可能会被外资所有，以挽救欧洲的就业机会——最新动态 德国汽车行业警告称，除非社会和工人接受需要“大胆决定”来应对来自中国和其他竞争对手的竞争，否则欧洲该行业的就业可能会崩溃。大众汽车准备正式提出最多裁员10万人，此举引发了一波抗议浪潮。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As the German car industry faces significant challenges and potential job losses, this news highlights the deep human impact of economic shifts on livelihoods and communities. Colossians 3:23 reminds us to approach all our work with diligence and integrity, as if serving Yahweh Himself, finding purpose and dignity in our labor even amidst uncertainty.
reflection.zh: 随着德国汽车工业面临严峻挑战和潜在的失业危机，这则新闻凸显了经济转型对生计和社区的深刻影响。歌罗西书3:23提醒我们，无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给雅伟做的，不是给人做的，这让我们在不确定性中也能在工作中找到目的和尊严。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: Plenty of players but no grassroots: can China ever grow into a footballing giant?
title.zh: 球员众多但缺乏基层：中国能否成长为足球巨头？

summary.en: Experts note that despite large crowds at amateur matches, China lacks a robust grassroots system to develop players into professionals, hindering its ambition to become a footballing giant.
summary.zh: 专家指出，尽管中国业余足球比赛吸引了大量观众，但缺乏健全的基层体系将球员培养成职业选手，这阻碍了其成为足球强国的雄心。

body.en: Some of its amateur matches pull in bigger crowds than European leagues but are more of a spectacle than a pathway to the professional game, say experts Michael Owen, a man who once quipped he had never drunk tea or coffee, isn’t known for his adventurous palate. Safe to assume, then, that the former England striker was out of his comfort zone sipping Roxburgh rose juice and eating chilli-wrapped rice noodle rolls during his recent visit to south-west China’s Guizhou province. The 2001 Ballon d’Or winner dusted off his boots for a match in Rongjiang county, the birthplace of viral amateur football league Cun Chao, also known as the Village Super League. Scoring twice in a 4-3 loss for local side Rongjiang Niubi, Owen endeared himself to the thousands in attendance, even if some weren’t familiar with the former Liverpool and Real Madrid player. Continue reading...
body.zh: 专家迈克尔·欧文(Michael Owen)表示，它的一些业余比赛比欧洲联赛吸引了更多的观众，但更多的是一场奇观，而不是进入职业比赛的途径。迈克尔·欧文曾打趣说自己从未喝过茶或咖啡，但他并不以冒险的味觉而闻名。那么，可以肯定的是，这位前英格兰前锋在最近访问中国西南部的贵州省期间，已经走出了自己的舒适区，喝着罗克斯堡玫瑰汁，吃着辣椒卷。这位2001年金球奖得主在榕江县的一场比赛中掸掉了靴子上的灰尘，那里是风靡一时的业余足球联赛存超（也称为乡村超级联赛）的发源地。在当地球队榕江牛鼻子队以4-3输球的比赛中，欧文梅开二度，赢得了数千名现场观众的喜爱，尽管有些人对这位前利物浦和皇家马德里球员并不熟悉。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The challenge of building a strong football culture from the ground up highlights the importance of foundational development. Just as a child needs careful guidance and training to flourish, so too does any endeavor require intentional investment in its earliest stages to achieve lasting success. This reminds us that true growth often begins with nurturing...
reflection.zh: 从基层建立强大足球文化的挑战，突显了基础发展的重要性。正如孩子需要细心引导和培养才能茁壮成长，任何事业也需要对其早期阶段进行有意识的投入，才能取得持久的成功。这提醒我们，真正的成长往往始于在基层培养潜力。

verse.textEn: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
verse.textZh: 教养孩童，使他走当行的道，就是到老他也不偏离。

title.en: Lethal tornado tears through Chinese province amid devastating storms – video
title.zh: 致命龙卷风席卷中国省份，破坏性风暴肆虐——视频

summary.en: Devastating storms, including a lethal tornado, have swept through China's Hubei province, resulting in at least 15 fatalities and the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of residents. Chinese leader Xi Jinping has called for comprehensive rescue efforts for those affected.
summary.zh: 毁灭性风暴，包括一场致命的龙卷风，席卷了中国湖北省，造成至少15人死亡，数十万人被疏散。中国领导人习近平已敦促“全力以赴”救援受灾民众。

body.en: Storms tore through China's Hubei province, killing at least 15 people, according to state media. Hundreds of thousands of people have also been evacuated as devastating storms hit the country. Chinese leader Xi Jinping has urged 'all out' efforts to rescue those affected
body.zh: 据官方媒体报道，暴风雨席卷了中国湖北省，造成至少 15 人死亡。由于毁灭性风暴袭击该国，数十万人也被疏散。中国领导人习近平敦促“全力以赴”救援受灾群众

reflection.en: In the face of devastating natural disasters like the storms in Hubei, our hearts go out to those who have lost loved ones and homes. During such overwhelming times, we are reminded that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. May all affected find comfort and assistance, knowing they are not alone in their suffering.
reflection.zh: 面对像湖北风暴这样的毁灭性自然灾害，我们的心与那些失去亲人和家园的人同在。在这样令人不知所措的时刻，我们被提醒雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。愿所有受影响的人都能找到安慰和帮助，知道他们并非独自承受痛苦。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: China's missile test builds on Pacific nuclear deterrence
title.zh: 中国导弹试验增强太平洋核威慑

summary.en: US allies in the Pacific have condemned China's recent intercontinental ballistic missile test, which Beijing described as routine. The test is seen as a demonstration of China's increasing military capabilities.
summary.zh: 太平洋地区的美国盟友谴责了中国最近进行的洲际弹道导弹试验，北京称之为“例行”测试。此次试验被视为中国展示其日益增长的军事能力。

body.en:
US allies in the Pacific condemned what Beijing has called a "routine" intercontinental ballistic missile test, which comes as China seeks to demonstrate its growing military capabilities.

On Monday, the Chinese Navy conducted a missile test in the South Pacific , with state media reporting that a nuclear submarine fired a missile carrying a dummy warhead into international waters.

The test quickly drew harsh criticism from US allies in the Pacific. Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the Chinese test was destabilizing for regional security. Japan called on China to reconsider its actions.

New Zealand said it does not want China to use the South Pacific as a testing ground for missiles. "We are deeply concerned about China's tests of nuclear-capable weapons in the South Pacific," Foreign Minister Winston Peters said in Wellington

During the Cold War, the US tested numerous nuclear weapons around the South Pacific's Bikini Atoll, which today is part of the Marshall Islands. Since World War II, the US has dominated the postwar security architecture in the Pacific region .

China's military buildup is now challenging this construct . Although official media have not released any details about the test, nationalist military experts are speculating on Chinese social media about how powerful the tested missile might have been.

"It is a submarine-launched intercontinental ballistic missile of the Julang (JL)-3 series," wrote Lieutenant Colonel Zhang Junshe a researcher with the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Naval Military Academic Research Institute.

The Julang-3, which means "Giant Wave-3" in English, is currently still under development.

It is said to have a maximum range of 12,000 kilometers (7,400 miles) and can carry multiple nuclear warheads. So far, three successful tests have been reported between 2018 and 2019.

"The target of this missile is not combat troops on the front lines, but strategic targets such as command centers, military bases, or energy infrastructure," Zhang wrote in his blog.

The "Giant Wave-3" is believed to have been launched from a Type 094 Jin-class nuclear-powered submarine. With a full crew of 120 sailors, the 135-meter-long submarine can sustain a submerged crew for at least 70 days. Currently, the Chinese Navy has six Type 094 submarines in service.

According to the Nuclear Threat Initiative, a Washington-based think tank, China operates an additional 59 nuclear-powered attack submarines in addition to the Jin-class submarines.

"Even if all other military weapons were to be put out of action, the Chinese submarine would still be fully capable of launching a nuclear counterstrike," Zhang wrote.

As early as September 2024, China had launched an intercontinental missile carrying a dummy warhead from the...
body.zh: 美国在太平洋的盟友谴责北京所谓的“例行”洲际弹道导弹试验，此次试验是在中国寻求展示其不断增长的军事能力之际进行的。 周一，中国海军在南太平洋进行了一次导弹试验，官方媒体报道称，一艘核潜艇向国际水域发射了一枚携带假弹头的导弹。 这次试验很快引起了美国太平洋盟友的严厉批评。澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤表示，中国的试验破坏了地区安全的稳定。日本呼吁中国重新考虑其行动。 新西兰表示不希望中国利用南太平洋作为导弹试验场。外交部长温斯顿·彼得斯在惠灵顿表示：“我们对中国在南太平洋进行核武器试验深感担忧” 冷战期间，美国在南太平洋比基尼环礁（今天是马绍尔群岛的一部分）周围测试了许多核武器。二战以来，美国一直主导着太平洋地区的战后安全架构。 中国的军力建设现在正在挑战这种结构。尽管官方媒体尚未公布有关此次测试的任何细节，但民族主义军事专家正在中国社交媒体上猜测测试的导弹的威力可能有多大。 中国人民解放军海军军事学术研究院研究员张军社中校写道：“这是巨狼（JL）-3系列潜射洲际弹道导弹。” Julang-3，英文意思是“Giant Wave-3”，目前仍在开发中。 据称其最大射程为12,000公里（7,400英里），可携带多枚核弹头。到目前为止，2018 年至 2019 年间已报告了三项成功的测试。 张在博客中写道：“这种导弹的目标不是前线的作战部队，而是指挥中心、军事基地或能源基础设施等战略目标。” 据信“巨浪3”是从一艘094型晋级核动力潜艇上发射的。这艘135米长的潜艇共有120名水手，可以让水下船员至少生存70天。目前，中国海军有6艘094型潜艇在役。 据华盛顿智库核威胁倡议组织称，除了晋级潜艇之外，中国还拥有59艘核动力攻击潜艇。 张写道：“即使所有其他军事武器都无法发挥作用，中国潜艇仍然完全有能力发动核反击。” 早在2024年9月，中国就从...发射了一枚携带假弹头的洲际导弹。

reflection.en: The news of missile tests highlights the ongoing global pursuit of security through military strength. Yet, the prophet Isaiah envisioned a future where nations would transform instruments of war into tools for peace, no longer training for conflict. This vision reminds us to pray for leaders to seek true security not in escalating arms, but in pathways of...
reflection.zh: 导弹试验的消息凸显了全球通过军事力量寻求安全的持续努力。然而，先知以赛亚曾预见一个未来，各国将把战争工具变为和平工具，不再为冲突而训练。这一愿景提醒我们为领袖祷告，愿他们不在军备竞赛中寻求真正的安全，而是在相互理解和裁军的道路上。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

title.en: How do Australia's 'great deals' with its neighbours compare to China?
title.zh: 澳大利亚与邻国的“大交易”与中国相比如何？

summary.en: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is strengthening diplomatic and economic ties with Pacific island nations, a region where China has significant influence.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯正在加强与太平洋岛国的外交和经济关系，该地区是中国具有重要影响力的区域。

body.en:
Anthony Albanese is turning his attention to the Solomon Islands after securing Australia a major new defence agreement with Fiji, as he seeks to shore up support against the expansion of Chinese influence in the region.

Albanese and Fijian Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka formalised the Ocean of Peace Alliance alongside an updated Vuvale Union partnership during a ceremony in the Fijian capital Suva on Monday.

Albanese hailed the treaties, aimed at strengthening regional security amid intensifying strategic competition in the Pacific, as "one of the most significant endeavours Australia has undertaken with any country".

Fiji is one of Australia's closest Pacific security partners and has one of the region's largest militaries, making the agreement one of Canberra's most noteworthy in the Pacific.

The visit to Suva is part of a days-long diplomatic mission during which Albanese will meet with several regional leaders including Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale for a whistle-stop tour on Tuesday, with the focus on a new comprehensive treaty.

The leaders last week agreed to start talks on a treaty to "capture the two countries' joint ambition for the relationship".

This latest push from Albanese comes as China confirmed on Monday it successfully tested a submarine-launched ballistic missile carried by a strategic nuclear submarine in international waters in the Pacific Ocean.

The agreements with Fiji expand the two nations' long-standing security and development relationship and introduce a mutual defence commitment.

The new Ocean of Peace Alliance commits both countries to consult and respond to security developments that threaten the sovereignty, peace or stability of either nation.

"Each Party recognises that an armed attack on any of the Parties within the Pacific would be dangerous to each other's peace and security as well as the security of the Pacific, and declares that it would act to meet the common danger, in accordance with its domestic processes," the deal reads.

Australia will support the partnership with more than $1 billion in funding over the next decade, targeting transnational crime prevention and investing in education, healthcare, and infrastructure projects in Fiji.

Australia works with all 14 Pacific Island nations to varying degrees, and has major security agreements with Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Tuvalu and Nauru.

It also cooperates with other nations in the region, from foreign aid and infrastructure funding to marine surveillance and peacekeeping.

title.en: 'Destabilising': Australia criticises China after ballistic missile test launch in the Pacific
title.zh: “破坏稳定”：澳大利亚批评中国在太平洋进行弹道导弹试验

summary.en: Australia has criticized China following a ballistic missile test launch in the Pacific, describing the action as "destabilising." This test marks China's latest intercontinental ballistic missile launch in 2024.

body.en:
Australia and New Zealand have sounded the alarm after China confirmed it successfully tested a ballistic missile carried by a strategic nuclear submarine in international waters in the Pacific Ocean.

Chinese state media Xinhua reported that the testing is part of China's annual military exercise, and it had alerted relevant countries in advance, in accordance with international law.

Xinhua described the launch as a "routine arrangement" of China's annual military training and said it was not directed against any specific country or target.

This comes after Australia and Fiji signed a major defence alliance earlier in the day, committing each country to come to the other's aid in case either is attacked.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the Australian government had been advised in advance by China of the test.

"Australia has been clear with China that we regard this as destabilising to the region," she told reporters on Monday, moments before the launch was confirmed.

"This proposed test is in the context of a rapid military buildup by China, which is lacking in the transparency and reassurance as to intent that the region expects."

Wong said the test was "inconsistent" with Pacific leaders' requests for the ocean to be one "of peace".

"It appears that, despite our long-standing concerns about this type of activity, China carried out the test within hours of informing us," he said in a statement.

"The Pacific is an Ocean of Peace and we are deeply concerned by China's testing of nuclear-capable weapons into the South Pacific."

Japan's government said it had been notified of the missile launch and urged China to reconsider.

"We expressed our grave concern over the Chinese military's increased activity," Tokyo said, adding that Japan's Coast Guard had been notified on Sunday by Chinese authorities about falling space debris that could fall within Japan's exclusive economic zone.

Japan's Kyodo news agency on Monday reported, citing a Japanese government source, that the missile had landed outside Japan's EEZ.

China's elite Rocket Force fired a dummy warhead into the sea near French Polynesia in September 2024, its first long-range missile launch over international waters in more than 40 years.

title.en: Court to deliver judgement on pianist sacked by Melbourne Symphony Orchestra over Gaza
title.zh: 法院将对墨尔本交响乐团因加沙问题解雇钢琴家作出判决

summary.en: The outcome of an international concert pianist's lawsuit for an alleged unfair dismissal over his comments on Gaza before a performance will be known on Friday.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Federal Court will deliver judgment on an alleged unfair dismissal of pianist Jayson Lloyd Gillham by the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra (MSO) over comments about Gaza on Friday.

In August 2024, the international concert pianist told a recital audience that Israel had deliberately targeted some journalists to prevent the reporting of war crimes, before playing a composition piece dedicated to Gazan journalists.

Gillham was sacked the next day, with the orchestra cancelling a subsequent concert at the Melbourne Town Hall, citing safety concerns.

Gillham's barrister Sheryn Omeri KC said the case was fundamentally about the right to freedom of expression for workers, and whether those rights could be limited by the implied term of a contract.

The pianist's comments were lawful and audience members who did not want to listen to them could have left the Southbank venue, she said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

But the MSO barrister Justin Bourke KC argued an unfettered right to free speech on the stage could have profound consequences, affecting ticket sales, sponsors and donors.

It would ultimately be unworkable, especially if an artist wanted to speak on stage for an hour, and the MSO was "entitled to have control" over its own stage, he said.

In oral evidence, Gillham agreed that he hadn't told the orchestra or his agent that he intended to play the piece titled Witness, as he worried they would have an excuse to disallow the performance.

The MSO argued Gillham would have anticipated people would be upset by his comments, with management responding to the incident within minutes.

The orchestra received one written and two verbal complaints after the concert, followed by 487 complaints about the cancellation decision, the court was told.

According to the United Nations, over 260 journalists have been killed in the Israel-Gaza war since October 7, 2023.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
More than six years after COVID-19 triggered a global pandemic, scientists are still discovering new details about how the virus behaves inside the human body.

Researchers from La Trobe University have uncovered a previously unknown pathway that allows SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, to infect immune cells, triggering a powerful inflammatory response that can lead to severe lung damage.

The study found SARS-CoV-2 can hide inside dying fragments of infected cells, allowing the virus to gain access to immune cells as they engulf cellular debris during the body's natural clean-up process.

Once inside the immune cells, known as macrophages, the virus can spread to other immune cells and trigger an inflammatory response that damages lung tissue.

Kha Phan, a National Health and Medical Research Centre emerging leadership fellow at the La Trobe Institute for Molecular Science, was lead researcher in the study.

He told SBS News the study had "uncovered a novel pathway of viral transmission".

"Our macrophages have a defence mechanism, so they get inflamed. They actually cause all of the defence mechanisms, triggering all the inflammation that we observe in COVID-19 patients," he said.

Phan said the discovery will help scientists improve their understanding of what drives severe COVID-19, which makes it easier to identify more targeted treatments that can dampen the body's response.

He said applying more effective treatments earlier could help to prevent long-term complications, such as long COVID, if the initial severity of inflammation can be reduced.

"This fundamentally shifts the way we think about viral infections and solves a long-standing puzzle about how COVID-19 infects immune cells and drives severe inflammation," Phan said.

Respiratory viruses such as COVID-19, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) continue to infect millions of people worldwide each year.

The World Health Organization estimates that the seasonal flu alone may lead to up to 650,000 deaths each year. More than seven million deaths due to COVID-19 have been reported globally since December 2019.

Phan said unknown transmission pathways could also exist in viral diseases like influenza and RSV that involve similar inflammatory processes.

"Understanding these mechanisms could help us develop more effective treatments and improve our preparedness for future viral outbreaks," he said.

summary.en: A brown huntsman is the quickest of more than 250 species analysed by scientists in the UK and Germany If arachnophobes were not frightened enough by the horrific ability of Australia’s huntsman spiders to drag dead mice up the sides of fridges, they now have another reason....

body.en:
If arachnophobes were not frightened enough by the horrific ability of Australia’s huntsman spiders to drag dead mice up the sides of fridges , they now have another reason.

One member of the huntsman family, the brown huntsman Heteropoda jugulans, was clocked as the quickest of more than 250 spider species analysed by a team of scientists in the UK and Germany.

Reaching a peak speed of 3.59 metres per second (13km/h or 8mph), the humble and hairy-legged huntsman appears to be faster than the current world record-holder , the Moroccan flic-flac spider and its comparatively pedestrian 1.7 m/s (they don’t so much run, as tumble down hill to reach that speed).

The scientists collected 162 different spider species – mostly from around London and the German city of Greifswald, but also from North America, southern Europe and Australia – and then measured their running speeds using cameras and gridded paper as the running track. The research has been submitted to a scientific journal.

They also added to their analysis other studies that had measured spider speed and, crucially, that included research supervised by Dr Christofer Clemente, an evolutionary biomechanist at the University of the Sunshine Coast in Queensland.

Clemente’s research was originally published in 2021 and aimed to understand the unique way that spiders get about.

But rather than go searching for what he thought would be the quickest spiders, Clemente said he just grabbed the ones that were the easiest to get.

“These were just spiders I found in the back yard,” Clemente said. “I could just go out with my head torch and see them on the grass.

“I am interested in how different animals of different sizes move and whether muscle might limit the speed at which animals can run,” he said.

“Spiders don’t move using just muscle – they use a combination of muscles to retract their limbs and hydraulic pressure to push them outwards.

The brown huntsman only lives along Australia’s east coast and is a common site in homes in south-east Queensland.

They are about the size of a hand, and while they are venomous, they very rarely bite humans and when they do, the effects are mild.

While the 3.59 m/s was the peak speed recorded by the huntsman, Clemente said this was only reached for a fraction of a second. The huntsman’s average sustained speed was closer to 2 m/s.

When it comes to running in the animal kingdom, he said generally there appeared to be a “sweet spot” between having legs and muscles that were long but “not so big that you have to support this huge mass”.

His hunch was that huntsmans “might be close to the sweet spot” for the best spider body type for speed.

“They’re not too big and not too small, but we haven’t done the science on that yet,” he said.

summary.en: Rivals in cricket, but allies in defence. Here's what the two nations have committed to.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及合一、和好与弥合分歧。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A handshake and a smile sealed the deal between Australia and its "top-tier" security partner, as Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, pledged to strengthen ties across trade, education, defence, science and technology.

" While we are separated by an ocean, we are indeed the closest of friends," Albanese told reporters in Canberra during a joint press statement.

"Australia values India as a top-tier security partner, and the Declaration reflects our shared commitment to a peaceful, stable and prosperous Indo-Pacific region."

References to cricket embraced the common ground between the two nations, with Modi likening their partnership to a "long and intense test match".

However, underneath the sports metaphors was an undercurrent of concern around the Indo-Pacific's defence challenges, with one eye on the fallout of war in Iran and economic disruptions, and the other on China, just days after it conducted a missile test in the Pacific .

Central to the agreement is the vision of a stable, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

To get there, Albanese and Modi both pledged to strengthen defence ties between the two nations.

While no new partnership was announced, the two leaders confirmed their commitment to existing defence pledges, the most recent being the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership established in 2020.

" We will boost strategic coordination, increase the complexity of our defence exercises and further build interoperability between our defence forces," Albanese said.

" We have endorsed a joint maritime security collaboration roadmap and agreed to a new Australia-India partnership on cyber, critical technologies and supply chains."

India and Australia have opened the door to greater aircraft deployment in each other's territories, and there will be more exchanges, education, and training between the defence personnel of each nation.

They will also increase information sharing on terrorist threats in the region, terrorist financing and online radicalisation.

The strengthening of defence ties comes just two days after China tested a nuclear-capable missile in the Pacific.

"There is no doubt that this is a provocative act by China which does destabilise the region," Albanese said at the time.

"Today we can confirm the signing of the administrative arrangement to export uranium to India for peaceful purposes under the 2015 Australia-India nuclear cooperative agreement," Albanese told reporters in Canberra.

title.en: Angus Taylor defends Liberal senator's triple zero test calls during Telstra outage
title.zh: 安格斯·泰勒为自由党参议员在澳洲电信停电期间的三零测试电话进行辩护

summary.en: Sarah Henderson's emergency service test is under scrutiny as Telstra says customers can now "feel confident" calling triple zero.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Opposition leader Angus Taylor has spoken out in defence of Liberal senator Sarah Henderson's decision to test whether or not she could contact triple zero during Wednesday's Telstra outage.

Sarah Henderson, the Opposition's communications spokesperson, made two calls to the triple zero network after the service was disrupted by the widespread outage that caused chaos across the country .

Making false calls to triple zero is a criminal offence with a maximum penalty of three years in prison, and Henderson's test calls have been criticised by Labor as irresponsible.

Australia's largest telecommunications company faced connectivity issues for a second day, as a separate issue prevented some users from contacting triple zero.

While major issues were largely resolved by Telstra at approximately mid-morning on Wednesday, some transport networks remain slow or at a standstill on Thursday.

Early on Thursday morning, the company said overnight work had reduced the separate triple zero error by about 90 per cent. On Thursday afternoon, it said it had "implemented a solution" that had addressed the issue, and customers could feel confident calling triple zero.

Taylor argued on Thursday that Henderson was doing her job as Coalition communications spokesperson and that her actions were not illegal.

"If [Communications Minister Anika Wells] hadn't been absent for seven hours, Sarah wouldn't have had to do these things," Taylor said.

"These actions were not illegal and they were made necessary by complete and utter failure from this minister and that should be the focus of the press, and it should be the focus of the nation."

The senator insisted she was within her rights to make the test calls on Thursday morning.

"I was simply, as the shadow minister for communications, making those initial calls to work out whether the ... system was actually operating," she told Sydney radio station 2GB.

"I accept the criticism, but what I will say is that I am in a unique position holding this government to account."

Industry Minister Tim Ayres said making the calls at a time when the emergency phone network was being impacted was reckless.

"I was absolutely shocked by that revelation. I just say to Australians, don't do what she did," he told ABC radio.

"It's utterly irresponsible. I just don't know why anybody would do that, but I'd certainly say nobody should follow her example."

Telstra's chief financial officer Michael Ackland said on Thursday that Telstra had completed more than 630 welfare checks during the outage for people who had called triple zero but failed to be connected.

title.en: Australian milk, Indian tea: Narendra Modi talks up Australian relationship in stadium address
title.zh: 阿尔巴尼斯和莫迪签署铀协议，数万人聚集迎接“重要”访问

summary.en: Australia and India have signed an agreement allowing Australia to export uranium to India. The deal specifies that the uranium is to be used solely for "peaceful purposes."
summary.zh: 澳大利亚和印度签署了一项协议，允许澳大利亚向印度出口铀。该协议明确规定，铀将仅用于“和平目的”。

body.en:
Taking a stage in front of thousands at Melbourne's Marvel Stadium, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi summed up the connection between the two countries with one striking image: " We Indians love to spread love... The milk at home might be Australian, but the tea brewed is Indian."

"The lentils and vegetables are Australian, yet they are tempered with authentic Indian spices," Modi said.

The stadium address on Thursday evening was part of Modi's three-day trip for the Australia-India Annual Leaders' Summit.

There were more empty seats than Modi's last stadium appearance in Australia , but the crowd was all smiles as Modi delivered a lengthy speech praising India's contribution to Australia's economy while promoting India's plan to be one of the world's top three economic powerhouses.

"In the last 12 years, I have come here for the third time. This time, a hat-trick has been scored! This reflects the heights that India-Australia relations have reached."

Using the English-language catchphrase of "Grow more! Achieve more!", Modi reiterated his vision of India as a rising global superpower. His aim, he said, was for India to become one of the top three global economies, citing rapid digital transformation and the country's 5G rollout as some of the achievements that pave the way for India's success.

"The India of the 21st century is working towards becoming a developed nation. When we realise one dream, new dreams take its place," he said.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joined Modi on the stage, with the two walking out together in good spirits.

A group of supporters of the Khalistan movement gathered to protest Modi's visit outside an event at Government House on Thursday.

The Khalistan movement broadly advocates for a separate homeland for Sikhs and has faced suppression by the Indian government.

Canberra India Council chair Deepak-Raj Gupta travelled to Melbourne with his wife and friends to attend as many Modi-related events as possible.

Modi is one of three types of people who are "very popular" in his homeland, Gupta said.

Pradeep Taneja, a senior lecturer in Asian politics at the University of Melbourne, said Modi's visit was "significant" and "unprecedented".

"No other Indian prime minister has been to Australia three times during his term in office," he told SBS News.

"The security relationship between Australia and India has grown much faster than I think other dimensions of the relationship. Australia now regards India as a top-tier — and I quote here, top-tier is the Australian government's language — a top-tier security partner."
